facts.statement: Aepyornithomimus lived around 75 million years ago in an area that was likely a desert.
facts.quote: It lived in the Campanian, around 75 million years ago, when the area is thought to have been a desert.

facts.statement: Aepyornithomimus was formally described in 2017 by a team of paleontologists including Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig and Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: MPC-D 100/130 was formally described in 2017 by paleontologists Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, Philip J. Currie, Mahito Watabe and Rinchen Barsbold

facts.statement: The genus name Aepyornithomimus means "Aepyornis mimic" and refers to the similar foot structure of the large ratite Aepyornis.
facts.quote: The generic name, Aepyornithomimus, is derived from the large ratites Aepyornis and the Latin mimus (meaning mimic), in reference to the similar foot structure.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Aepyornithomimus shows an intermediate metatarsal condition between basal and more derived ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: Morphologically, observations were made that it seemed transitional between the metatarsal condition in basal ornithomimosaurs and more derived ones, and it was suggested that A. tugikinensis shows an intermediate condition.

facts.statement: Aepyornithomimus is the first diagnostic ornithomimosaur found in early, dry deposits, suggesting the group could tolerate various environmental conditions.
facts.quote: A. tugrikinensis is the first diagnostic ornithomimosaur found in these earlier, drier deposits, and indicates the group could tolerate a variety of environmental conditions.

facts.statement: Aepyornithomimus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 70 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del periodo Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83 y 70 millones de años atrás durante el Campaniense en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aepyornithomimus are found in Late Cretaceous rocks of the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encuentran en rocas del Cretácico Superior de la Formación Djadochta en Mongolia.

facts.statement: The Djadochta Formation where Aepyornithomimus was found was an arid eolian desert similar to the modern Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: La formación Djadokhta donde se encontró Aepyornithomimus era un desierto árido eólico similar al moderno Desierto de Gobi.

facts.statement: Aepyornithomimus belongs to the infraorder Ornithomimosauria.
Aepyornithomimus is classified within the family Ornithomimidae.
